title: Cap. VI Arg. 1: Augustine — praedestinatio is foresight and preparation of God's benefits
pass_a_gloss: The first argument will be sought from the various definitions of Predestination, Augustine defining; Predestination is the foresight and preparation of the benefits of God, by which whoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. Where it is to be observed that God foreknows those benefits or gifts of grace, by which applied he himself will liberate certain singular elect persons; then, prepares all these for them, and at length, as he foresaw and prepared, confers them at the opportune time. What can be thought here that does not flow from the mere good pleasure of God, preceding every act of the human will? For God foresaw in the elect those gifts of grace which he himself predestinated and prepared for them according to his free benevolence, when he elected them in Christ. As is also openly gathered from the Apostle Ephes. 1:3–4. &c. If anyone here, that he may pour darkness upon the pure mercy of God, put forward foresight faith as having been a cause, or antecedent condition, he will have dealt in trifles; since faith is one of the chief of these benefits which in the decree of predestination are prepared for elect men.
pass_b_english: First argument: from various definitions of Predestination. Augustine: Predestination is the foresight and preparation of God's benefits, by which whoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. Observe: God foreknows those benefits or grace-gifts by which, applied, he will liberate certain singular elect persons; then prepares them all for them; and at length, as he foresaw and prepared, confers them at the right time. What here does not flow from God's mere good pleasure, preceding every act of the human will? He foresaw in the elect those grace-gifts he himself predestinated and prepared by free benevolence when he elected them in Christ — as Eph. 1:3–4 also openly shows. To cast darkness on pure divine mercy by putting foresight faith as cause or antecedent condition is trifling — faith is one of the chief benefits prepared for the elect in the predestination decree.
source_text: Primum argumentum petetur a definitionibus Praedestinationis variis, definiente Augustino; Praedestinatio est praescientia et praeparatio beneficiorum Dei, quibus certissime liberantur quicunque liberantur. Ubi observandum, Deum praescire ea beneficia sive gratiae dona, quibus adhibitis ipse liberabit singulares quasdam personas electas; dein, haec omnia illis praeparare, ac tandem, sicut praescivit et praeparavit, opportuno tempore conferre. Quid hic cogitari potest, quod non dimanet a mero Dei beneplacito, omnem humanae voluntatis actum praecedente? Praescivit enim Deus in electis illa dona gratiae quae ipse illis praedestinavit et praeparavit secundum gratuitam suam benevolentiam, quando illos elegit in Christo. Ut aperte etiam ex Apostolo colligitur Ephes. i. 3–4. &c. Si quis hic, ut purae Dei misericordiae tenebras offundat, praevisam fidem obtendat fuisse causam, aut conditionem antecedaneam, nugas egerit; cum fides sit unum ex praecipuis hisce beneficiis quae in praedestinationis decreto praeparantur hominibus electis.
